data.summary: When [agent].family is unset, _order_cross_family_first degenerates to config order, so the review record names a same-family identifying reviewer (lan-deepseek-v4-pro) instead of the clean cross-family reviewer (gemini/google or grok/xai) whose findings are on record. complete --model deepseek then refuses "reviewer independence not satisfied", blocking every bug complete on a lane. Root cause in the identifying-reviewer resolution (which reviewer is NAMED identifying for independence), a separate defect from the dispatch order fix B19066e802f.
data.title: identifying reviewer resolves same-family as the author, blocking complete even when grok/gemini reviewed clean

data.body:
Fixes bug B2e5ca93520: When [agent].family is unset, _order_cross_family_first degenerates to config order, so the review record names a same-family identifying reviewer (lan-deepseek-v4-pro) instead of the clean cross-family reviewer (gemini/google or grok/xai) whose findings are on record. complete --model deepseek then refuses "reviewer independence not satisfied", blocking every bug complete on a lane. Root cause in the identifying-reviewer resolution (which reviewer is NAMED identifying for independence), a separate defect from the dispatch order fix B19066e802f.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B2e5ca93520 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B2e5ca93520 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B2e5ca93520: identifying reviewer resolves same-family as the author, blocking complete even when grok/gemini...

data.claim: With brief item=X, the RESUME slice renders up to 5 unrelated crashed items and places the item own entry alphabetically among them, so the reserved block eats the budget and the focused item detail becomes a cut notice.
data.falsifier: _brief_recovery(out, recovery, item=FOCUS) already renders FOCUS first and collapses unrelated entries to a count, so tests/test_brief_recovery_focus.py would PASS on the current code.
data.mechanism: _brief_recovery sorts by (kind, item) and renders the whole per-band list OUTSIDE the budget; it does not know the focused item and expands unrelated entries to the per-band cap.
data.probe: uv run pytest tests/test_brief_recovery_focus.py -q
data.probe_output: 3 failed: TypeError _brief_recovery() got an unexpected keyword argument item on the unfixed code.
data.question: Does the brief RESUME slice crowd out the focused item detail when an item is given?

evidence.note: tests/test_brief_recovery_focus.py: uv run pytest -q -> 3 failed (TypeError: _brief_recovery() got an unexpected keyword argument item) on unfixed code; research R032db0e051 CONFIRMED

chunk_findings.detail: The focused-item collapse is gated on `if own:` after `_own_recovery(bands, item)`. When a brief is for a focused item that does not itself appear in `recovery`, `own` is empty, so the fallback `else` renders up to `_RECOVERY_SHOWN` entries per band exactly as before. Input: `item="UX-output-caps"` with 5 unrelated recovery entries and no `UX-output-caps` recovery entry. The RESUME block still lists all 5 lines, so `Current` / `Ready now` can still be cut. This contradicts the new docstring promise that, with an item given, every unrelated entry collapses to a count, and leaves the reported bug unfixed for the no-own-entry case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown/briefing.py:_brief_recovery

chunk_findings.detail:
The test named `test_focused_items_own_entry_comes_first_and_others_collapse_to_a_count` never actually verifies that the focused item’s own entry comes first. It only asserts that `**FOCUS**` is present, that `**W0**` is absent, and that the string `"5 other recoverable entries"` is present. An implementation that renders the collapsed count line before the focused entry, for example:

```
## ⚠ RESUME: recoverable work found
5 other recoverable entries
**FOCUS** (expired_lease ...
```

would satisfy every assertion, even though it violates the “own entry renders FIRST” requirement. The regression test can therefore be green while the ordering bug remains.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_brief_recovery_focus.py:34

chunk_findings.detail: When `item` is non-empty but that id is not in any recovery band, `_own_recovery` returns `[]` and the `else` branch still emits the full per-band list (up to `_RECOVERY_SHOWN` entries per band, each with a resume line). Input: `item="UX-output-caps"` and five unrelated holding recoveries, none named UX-output-caps. Those five lines are still reserved and still crowd Current/Ready into `[N more cut]`, which is the bug this change claims to close. The docstring promises that a brief about one item collapses unrelated entries to a count; that only happens if `own` is non-empty. `test_no_focus_keeps_the_per_band_cap` locks this in by passing `item="T9"` (a focus with no entry) and asserting `**W0**` through `**W4**` still render.
chunk_findings.title: `_brief_recovery`

chunk_findings.detail: The test named for “comes first” never checks order. `**FOCUS**` anywhere in the block, plus the count line and the absence of `**W0**`, still passes if the count is emitted above the focused entry. A reorder that puts unrelated summary text ahead of the crash being resumed would not fail this regression.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds. The new `if own:` branch now renders only the focused item’s own recovery entry and collapses every unrelated recovery into a single count line, but the user-facing block header still reads: `This section is OUTSIDE the brief token budget, so it lists every entry.` With `item="UX-output-caps"` and one own recovery plus five unrelated recoverable entries, the block lists only the own entry and `- _5 other recoverable entries..._`, so the header’s promise is false. The author’s triage says the docstring was fixed, but that does not update the header line shown to users.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown/briefing.py:_brief_recovery RESUME header

chunk_findings.detail: `_render` only calls `_brief_recovery` and asserts the lines that helper appends. None of the tests run the full `ddflow brief item=...` budget path and check that Current/Ready now/decisions/memory no longer collapse to `[N more cut]`. An implementation can pass all these local string checks while the outer brief still reserves the whole token slice for RESUME, so the actual user-visible bug is not regression-tested.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test meant to prove that every OTHER recovery entry collapses to one count line only asserts `W0` is absent. With the same five other entries, an incorrect `_brief_recovery` that hides only `W0` while still expanding `W1`–`W4` and also emits a `5 other recoverable entries` line would pass, leaving four unrelated recoveries expanded before Current — the budget-eats-brief behavior is not fully guarded.

chunk_findings.detail: The fix only collapses unrelated recoveries when the focused item is itself in the recovery list (`if own:`). If a user runs `ddflow brief item=<some-item>` for an item that has no recovery entry, `_own_recovery(bands, item)` returns `[]`, so the `else` branch still renders up to `_RECOVERY_SHOWN` entries per band plus one “more” line per band. For example, with `item="Other"` and 5 unrelated crashed worktrees, RESUME still emits multiple entry/resume status lines, and Current/Ready now/decisions/memory can still collapse to `[N more cut]`. That leaves B-brief-recover-eats-budget unfixed for any item-specific brief whose item is not itself among the recovery entries, even though the intent says unrelated entries should be counted when an item is given.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown/briefing.py:_brief_recovery

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #2 still holds: the end-to-end regression only asserts `assert "## Current: T9" in text`, but the reported bug is that the Current section’s body collapses to `[N more cut]`. A broken implementation that keeps the `## Current: T9` header and replaces its detail with `[N more cut]` would pass this assertion, so it does not prove the user-visible symptom is gone. The test also never sets the 1200-token budget from the bug report or creates enough content to hit the default budget. It should assert that the Current section body is not a `[N more cut]` placeholder, or that T9’s own detail text is actually present.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_brief_recovery_focus.py:test_the_full_brief_counts_unrelated_and_keeps_the_current_section

chunk_findings.detail: The full-brief regression added for B-brief-recover-eats-budget still does not lock the budget failure it claims to close. `test_the_full_brief_counts_unrelated_and_keeps_the_current_section` only asserts `"## Current: T9" in text`. The reported bug is that Current, Ready now, decisions, and memory remain as named sections whose bodies are only `[N more cut]` lines. A brief that still prints that heading and then cuts the body (and never renders Ready now / decisions / memory content) satisfies this assertion. The RESUME count checks can pass after the collapse fix while the token slice is still spent before those sections, so the test would not fail the unfixed budget behavior the comment says it guards.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_brief_recovery_focus.py:109

chunk_findings.detail: The RESUME constant is `"## ⚠ RESUME: recoverable work found"`, but the actual `_brief_recovery` header recorded in the previous triage is exactly `## RESUME: recoverable work found` with no `⚠`. That string never occurs in the rendered block, so every local test fails immediately at `assert RESUME in text`, and the full-path test fails at `text.index(RESUME)`. The added tests are all red before exercising the fix.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_brief_recovery_focus.py:18

chunk_findings.detail: The end-to-end test uses the document title as the end marker: `end = text.index("# ddflow brief")`. The full brief text begins with that H1, so `end` is 0, which is before the RESUME heading. The slice `text[text.index(RESUME) : end]` is therefore the empty string, and the next line `region.index("**T9**")` raises `ValueError` before any of the intended end-to-end assertions run. Use `len(text)` or an actual end marker after the RESUME block.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_brief_recovery_focus.py:end = text.index("# ddflow brief")

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 2 still holds in part: the new full-brief test does not reproduce the 1200-token budget condition and only asserts that the `## Current: T9` heading exists. An implementation could still emit `## Current: T9` followed by `[N more cut]` and pass, leaving the reported user-visible bug unguarded. The test should set the same budget cap and assert absence of `[N more cut]` inside Current (and ideally the other cut sections), not merely the heading.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_brief_recovery_focus.py:assert "## Current: T9" in text

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier gap is only half closed. `test_the_full_brief_counts_unrelated_and_keeps_the_current_section` does run `LC.brief`, but the only proof that the token budget was not eaten is `assert "## Current: T9" in text`. The reported failure mode is a Current (and Ready now / decisions / memory) section whose body is only `[N more cut]`, which still contains that heading. Given a brief whose RESUME slice still reserves the whole budget, this assertion passes while the focused item's detail stays cut, so the regression does not fail on the unfixed budget behavior.
